clue.text: A true involvement with red rubies might with spadework bring it to light

definitions.text: might with spadework bring it to light

indicators.note: involvement means the letters are tangled together and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Digging through a red-ruby hoard reveals a hidden trove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement with' tells you to mix the letters of A TRUE with RED RUBIES; the fourteen letters make the two-word answer that a spade might uncover.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate's hoard dug into the ground is exactly what spadework would bring back to light.

clue.text: Is he in the troop or excluded from it?.

indicators.note: in means the words is he are placed inside the word for a troop

parts.note: a band is a troop or company of people

explanation.surface: A question about whether a soldier belongs to the troop or has been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished has been sent away and shut out from a group.

clue.text: Rule broken by a stupid fellow put into a different post

indicators.note: broken by means the word for rule is split open with another piece set inside

parts.note: to reign is to rule
an ass is a stupid fellow

explanation.surface: A ruler deposed by an idiot is moved to another job.
explanation.definitionFit: To move someone to a new job is to give them a fresh assignment.

clue.text: At heart we feel sure they're difficult to grasp

indicators.note: at heart says the answer sits in the middle of the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone confesses deep down that something is hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery fish are famously hard to hold onto.

clue.text: See 1
Gem of a fellow, despite his lack of the social graces

definitions.text: Gem of a fellow, despite his lack of the social graces

parts.words: Gem of a fellow, despite his lack of the social graces
parts.note: an uncut precious stone, read as a good-hearted man with coarse manners

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an uncut gemstone and, figuratively, a kindly person lacking polish.

clue.text: A very old city with a subtle emanation

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city gives off a faint mystical glow.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a subtle atmosphere or glow surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Apprehensive of difficulty?

explanation.definitionFit: It means anxious, and read as un-easy it also means not easy, that is, hard.

clue.text: A boy saint pursuing a bird of prey

indicators.note: pursuing means the saint comes after the bird, so it is placed second

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: A holy man chases a hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Not quite the sort of man who is belted in New York .

indicators.note: in means the nobleman sits inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.words: the sort of man who is belted
parts.note: a belted earl wears a sword belt at investiture

explanation.surface: Someone almost gets beaten up in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belted' suggests being hit, but it refers to the belt an earl receives when created.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and not quite are synonyms.

clue.text: Four-pounders destined to be cut to pieces? :

definitions.text: Four-pounders destined to be cut to pieces?

parts.words: Four-pounders destined to be cut to pieces?
parts.note: bread baked as four-pound items, which will be sliced up; the first word suggests cutting into fourths

explanation.definitionFit: A quartern loaf was a standard British bread weighing about four pounds.

clue.text: The I and 4 the pirate didn't put on his tax return?

definitions.text: The I and 4 the pirate didn't put on his tax return?

parts.words: The I and 4 the pirate didn't put on his tax return?
parts.note: the pirate's dug-in loot from the clue at 1 and 4 is also undeclared income

explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is the OCR reading of 1: the pirate's loot from 1 and 4 across is also money kept away from the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealed riches describe both buried loot and income kept from the tax authorities.

clue.text: Indifferent pair of recidivist ducks

indicators.note: pair of means the piece is written down twice
a recidivist goes back to old ways, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a duck is a zero in cricket, the letter O, so ducks are Os

explanation.surface: Two repeat-offender ducks seem unimpressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre or middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Something one is entitled to correct?

explanation.definitionFit: It is an entitlement and also means accurate.

clue.text: Trees that are full of venom

explanation.definitionFit: Asp is an old name for the aspen tree and also a venomous snake.

clue.text: In any case no trouble

indicators.note: case means the word any encloses the next word like a container

explanation.surface: No problem at all, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother or irritate someone is to trouble them.

clue.text: Got to know about a lot of transferable stock?

indicators.note: about means the herd goes round the letter a

parts.note: livestock that can be moved and sold makes up a herd

explanation.surface: Someone learnt about a large parcel of shares changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like stock-market shares, but it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear of something is to learn it.

clue.text: One of BR's training directors

parts.note: BR is British Rail; a train's director is the person at its controls

explanation.definitionFit: The person at a locomotive's controls steers the train.

clue.text: Kept showing restraint in manner

explanation.definitionFit: Booked or held back, and also reticent or undemonstrative.

clue.text: Sad peers cruelly calumniated

indicators.note: cruelly signals the letters are treated roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Unhappy nobles were viciously slandered.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to slander, the same as calumniate.

clue.text: Achieving wonderful success in unravelling loving dreams

indicators.note: unravelling means the letters are untangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds brilliantly by working through romantic fantasies.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing wonders means having remarkable success.

clue.text: Degree held by academics of immense importance to Soviet heavy industry

definitions.text: of immense importance to Soviet heavy industry

indicators.note: held by means the degree is contained inside the academics

parts.note: dons are university teachers
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Graduates employed by universities matter greatly to Soviet industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the Donets coal basin was central to Soviet heavy industry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Donets Basin's coal and steel powered much of the Soviet economy.

clue.text: A Northerner rising in alarm

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman gets up in a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

clue.text: Multiplicity of noughts north of Oxford

parts.note: nought times nought written as O X O, the X a multiplication sign

explanation.surface: Many zeros are found up north from Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire or Oxford University.

clue.text: A capital creature that buzzes round the fleet

indicators.note: round means the insect surrounds the navy abbreviation

parts.note: a bee buzzes
RN, the Royal Navy, is the fleet

explanation.surface: A bee circles the ships in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Berne is the capital city of Switzerland.

clue.text: Are no longer a feature of Lower Egypt

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Things that have gone from the Nile delta.
explanation.definitionFit: Were is the past tense, so it says things exist no more.

clue.text: Rodolfo found her extremely frigid!

parts.note: in Puccini's opera La Bohème the poet Rodolfo sings that his beloved's tiny hand is frozen

explanation.definitionFit: Mimì is the heroine of La Bohème, whose cold hand Rodolfo warms.

clue.text: She gets all upset about nothing

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the zero
upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman is distraught over nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Lola is a woman's name.

clue.text: Husband put in vile old French prison

indicators.note: put in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: base means low or vile
to husband land is to farm it, to till

explanation.surface: A husband is locked away in a nasty French jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' reads as a spouse, but it is the verb meaning to cultivate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789.

clue.text: See 10
Sing and then swing once a week

indicators.note: swing means the letters are swung about into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer performs and then dances to swing music every week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the word as old-fashioned: it was formerly the word for a week.
explanation.definitionFit: Sennight is an archaic contraction of seven nights, a seven-day period.

clue.text: Put ashore and shown the way around?

indicators.note: around means the guided word is wrapped around and

parts.note: led means guided or shown the way

explanation.surface: Someone was dropped on shore and given directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or passengers landed are brought onto dry land from a ship.
